title: Effects of a change in occlusion on biomechanical parameters and performance in sport-specific movement patterns
summary: Investigating how changes in the way teeth are clenched affect certain movements in various sports. Biomecanical measurement systems are used to record which areas of the body or movements are most or least affected

interventions.name: These are active, athletic individuals - male and female - who are subjectively healthy and free of acute complaints in the craniomandibular or musculoskeletal system. The aim of this study is to analyse the effects of an altered bite (either caused by a splint or by removable aids, such as a cotton

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male and female athletically active participants
- For team sports: member of a team that is in the 1st, 2nd or 3rd Bundesliga or Oberliga and trains at least 3 times/week for at least 1.5 hours excluding competitive matches
-For individual sports between 10-20 hours/week depending on the sport
- According to subjective assessment, no health problems that restrict the performance of sport-specific movement sequences or the production and wearing of an occlusion splint
Exclusion criteria:
- Operations in the musculoskeletal or craniomandibular system within the last 
       2 years
- Acute complaints or injuries or illnesses in the musculoskeletal system or in the   
      craniomandibular system  
- Current physiotherapeutic, orthopaedic or orthodontic therapy
- Use of muscle relaxants
- Physically incorrect posture diagnosed by a doctor
